peers.name: azure-diagnostics
peers.description: Debug Azure production issues using AppLens, Azure Monitor, resource health, and safe triage, including evidence-only diagnosis without live access. WHEN: debug production issues, troubleshoot app service, app service high CPU, app service deployment failure, troubleshoot container apps, container app 503 or target port mismatch, troubleshoot functions, function telemetry missing or stopped after a config/connection-string change, troubleshoot AKS, VM RDP, Linux SSH, VM black screen, can't connect to VM, reset VM password, NSG or firewall blocking, kubectl cannot connect, kube-system/CoreDNS failures, pod pending, crashloop, node not ready, upgrade failures, analyze logs, KQL, insights, image pull failures, cold start issues, health probe failures, resource health, root cause of errors, troubleshoot event hubs, troubleshoot service bus, messaging SDK error, AMQP connection failure, message lock lost, lock renewal during long-running processing, service bus dead letter.

peers.name: azure-prepare
peers.description: Prepare azd-based Azure projects for deployment: generates azure.yaml, infrastructure (Bicep/Terraform), and Dockerfiles for the Azure Developer CLI (azd) workflow. USE ONLY when the user explicitly wants to use azd as the deployment tool, or the project already has an azure.yaml file. DO NOT USE FOR: non-azd deployments, Python App Service code-only deploys (use python-appservice-deploy), or cross-cloud migration (use azure-cloud-migrate). WHEN: prepare app for azd, create azure.yaml, set up azd infrastructure, modernize app for Azure with azd, deploy with azd, function app, timer trigger, service bus trigger, event-driven function, managed identity, generate Bicep, generate Terraform, create and deploy to Azure.

peers.name: azure-ai
peers.description: Build and troubleshoot Azure AI Search, Speech, Document Intelligence, Content Understanding, Translator, Content Safety, and OpenAI apps. WHEN: AI Search, vector search, hybrid search, semantic search, indexer, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, fast or batch transcription, Speech SDK logs, session ID, result ID, OCR, document translation, glossary.

peers.name: azure-deploy
peers.description: Execute Azure deployments for ALREADY-PREPARED applications that have existing .azure/deployment-plan.md and infrastructure files. DO NOT use this skill when the user asks to CREATE a new application — use azure-prepare instead. This skill runs azd up, azd deploy, terraform apply, and az deployment commands with built-in error recovery. Requires .azure/deployment-plan.md from azure-prepare and validated status from azure-validate. WHEN: \"run azd up\", \"run azd deploy\", \"execute deployment\", \"push to production\", \"push to cloud\", \"go live\", \"ship it\", \"bicep deploy\", \"terraform apply\", \"publish to Azure\", \"launch on Azure\". DO NOT USE WHEN: \"create and deploy\", \"build and deploy\", \"create a new app\", \"set up infrastructure\", \"create and deploy to Azure using Terraform\" — use azure-prepare for these.

en.tagline: Build, deploy and evaluate Foundry agents and models
en.summary: This skill helps developers work with Microsoft Foundry resources. It covers model deployment, the full development lifecycle of AI agents, evaluation workflows, and troubleshooting. It routes each request to a matching sub-skill with its own steps.
problem: Work on Foundry involves many separate tasks: creating a project, deploying a model, building an agent, evaluating it, and fixing failures. Each task has its own tools, prerequisites, and order of steps.
With this skill, the agent loads the matching sub-skill for the task and follows its steps. Dependency checks run first, and azd commands follow the shared azd guidance.
fit: Building, deploying, or updating a hosted Foundry agent with azd
Running batch or continuous evaluations and prompt optimization on an agent
Fine-tuning models with SFT, DPO, or RFT, or deploying a model with quota and region checks
unfit: General Azure deployment that is not Foundry-specific (use azure-deploy)
Azure Functions, App Service, or general Azure preparation (use azure-prepare)
steps: Run the dependency check and setup script before any workflow starts.
Match the user request to a workflow using the intent tables in SKILL.md.
Read the matching sub-skill document before calling any workflow-specific tools.
Read the azd guidance before running any azd command.
Use the Foundry MCP tools for discovery and workflow actions described in the sub-skill.
Keep local agent state, such as metadata and eval caches, inside the agent's `.foundry/` folder.

zh.tagline: 用于构建、部署和评估 Foundry 智能体与模型
zh.summary: 该技能帮助开发者使用 Microsoft Foundry 资源，涵盖模型部署、AI 智能体的完整开发流程、评估工作流和故障排查。它会把每个请求分派给对应的子技能，并按其步骤执行。
problem: 在 Foundry 上工作涉及多项独立任务：创建项目、部署模型、构建智能体、评估及修复故障。每项任务都有各自的工具、前置条件和操作顺序。
使用该技能后，智能体会为任务加载对应的子技能并按其步骤执行。系统会先做依赖检查，azd 命令则遵循共享的 azd 指南。
fit: 使用 azd 构建、部署或更新托管的 Foundry 智能体
对智能体运行批量或持续评估，以及提示词优化
微调 SFT、DPO 或 RFT 模型，或部署模型并检查配额和区域
unfit: 与 Foundry 无关的通用 Azure 部署（请使用 azure-deploy）
Azure Functions、App Service 或通用 Azure 准备工作（请使用 azure-prepare）
steps: 在开始任何工作流之前，先运行依赖检查和安装脚本。
根据 SKILL.md 中的意图表，把用户请求匹配到对应的工作流。
在调用任何工作流专用工具之前，先阅读对应的子技能文档。
在运行任何 azd 命令之前，先阅读 azd 指南。
按子技能的说明，使用 Foundry MCP 工具进行资源发现和执行工作流操作。
将本地智能体状态（如元数据和评估缓存）保存在该智能体的 `.foundry/` 文件夹内。
